name: Approve investments and dispositions at the Portfolio Execution Committee
summary: The Portfolio Execution Committee, chaired by the Chief Investment Officer, decides on new private investments, follow-ons, fund commitments, manager engagements and dispositions that exceed department authority. A secretariat checks each memo and its approval tier, Total Fund Management checks mandate fit, Risk adds an independent opinion, and members read the package before a weekly meeting where the sponsoring department presents. Most items are approved, often with conditions; some are deferred for more work, a few are declined, and the largest go to the Board. Waiting for the risk opinion and the next meeting slot takes most of the elapsed time, and bid deadlines force special meetings.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund manager with a management investment committee under delegated authorities and Board approval of the largest transactions.
baseline.notes: The committee was the Investment Decision Committee chaired by the Head of International in F2021 and became the Portfolio Execution Committee chaired by the CIO in F2022; the steps are the same.

trigger: A deal team submits an investment memo or exit proposal that exceeds department authority.
end_state: The decision is approved and recorded, declined, withdrawn, or recommended to the Board.

volume.seasonality: Heavier before calendar year end and fiscal year end (March) when sale processes close.

evidence.note: Process map estimate. Upstream processes would send about 60 memos a month at typical conversion rates, so about a quarter are assumed to be approved within department authority.

systems.name: Document management and investment committee memo repository
Deal pipeline and relationship management system
Risk analytics platform (potential loss, limits, stress tests)

steps.name: Log memo and open committee item
steps.description: The secretariat receives the memo from the deal team, opens an item in the committee tracker with deal name, department, amount and requested decision, and files the memo in the repository.

evidence.note: Every PEC item starts from a memo. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Check completeness and approval tier
steps.description: The secretariat checks the memo against the template (tax, legal, ESG and climate sections, sign-offs), reads the amount against the Investment Management Authorities to confirm the PEC or Board tier, and flags missing items.

error.defect_description: Approval tier misread, for example a follow-on aggregated wrongly.

control.basis: Investment Management Authorities set by the CEO: transaction approval tiers

evidence.note: Approval authorities by tier are set in the Investment Management Authorities. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Chase deal team for missing items
steps.description: The secretariat emails the deal lead listing the missing sections or sign-offs and follows up until the revised memo arrives.

evidence.note: Common practice for committee secretariats. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Assess mandate fit and total fund impact
steps.description: A TFM principal checks the deal against the department's mandate and capital allocation, its effect on exposure targets, leverage and liquidity, and writes a short portfolio fit note for the committee.

error.defect_description: Exposure or capacity figure taken from a stale allocation report.

evidence.note: The PEC evaluates whether investments are aligned to the mandate of the active strategy. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Review portfolio fit note
steps.description: A TFM managing director reads the note, adjusts the conclusion on capacity or mandate fit and approves it for the package.

evidence.note: Review layer is the author's assumption. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Obtain the independent risk opinion
steps.description: The secretariat waits for the risk team's written opinion on market, credit, liquidity and concentration effects and attaches it to the item. Occasionally the deal team withdraws the item because the sale process moves on.

control.basis: Integrated Risk Framework and Risk Policy: independent second-line risk view before approval

evidence.note: Risk independently measures risks and reports to the ISRC and its subcommittees. Wait for the parallel risk review is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Book an agenda slot
steps.description: The secretariat checks the deal timetable against the meeting calendar, books the item into the next regular meeting or, for a bid deadline, asks the chair's office for a special meeting.

evidence.note: Special meetings for time-critical approvals also occur at Board level (F2022). Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Arrange a special meeting and send the package
steps.description: For a deal with a bid deadline the secretariat finds a slot with enough members for quorum, sends the package the same day and confirms attendance.

evidence.note: Fast approval routes exist at peers. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Assemble and distribute the pre-read package
steps.description: The secretariat combines the memo, risk opinion, portfolio fit note and appendices into the meeting package, posts it to the repository and sends it to members before the meeting.

evidence.note: Materials are circulated before committee meetings at peers. Wait to the next meeting cycle is the author's estimate for a weekly committee.

steps.name: Private Equity head presents the item
steps.description: The Private Equity department head, with the deal lead, presents the memo at the meeting, summarises the thesis, price, risks and the requested approval, and answers members' questions on the deal.

evidence.note: Department heads sit on the cross-functional committee; the wait is the pre-read period before the meeting. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Real Assets head presents the item
steps.description: The Real Assets department head, with the deal lead, presents the memo at the meeting, summarises the thesis, price, risks and the requested approval, and answers members' questions on the deal.

evidence.note: Department heads sit on the cross-functional committee; the wait is the pre-read period before the meeting. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Credit Investments head presents the item
steps.description: The Credit Investments department head, with the deal lead, presents the memo at the meeting, summarises the thesis, price, risks and the requested approval, and answers members' questions on the deal.

evidence.note: Department heads sit on the cross-functional committee; the wait is the pre-read period before the meeting. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Active Equities head presents the item
steps.description: The Active Equities department head, with the deal lead, presents the memo at the meeting, summarises the thesis, price, risks and the requested approval, and answers members' questions on the deal.

evidence.note: Department heads sit on the cross-functional committee; the wait is the pre-read period before the meeting. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Capital Markets and Factor Investing head presents the item
steps.description: The Capital Markets and Factor Investing department head, with the deal lead, presents the memo at the meeting, summarises the thesis, price, risks and the requested approval, and answers members' questions on the deal.

evidence.note: Department heads sit on the cross-functional committee; the wait is the pre-read period before the meeting. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Members review pre-read and question the team
steps.description: Committee members read the package before the meeting and question the deal team on price, downside cases and fit. This step carries the combined time of about four members other than the chair, risk, legal and finance.

evidence.note: Sub-committees are composed of cross-functional Global Leadership Team members. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Risk head gives the risk view
steps.description: The head of Risk summarises the risk opinion, the effect on total fund risk and limits, and any conditions Risk recommends.

control.basis: Three lines model: independent risk function separate from the investment department

evidence.note: Independent risk reporting to ISRC subcommittees. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: General Counsel reviews legal and reputational issues
steps.description: The General Counsel reads the legal, regulatory, sanctions and reputational sections and raises conditions such as foreign investment review or structure changes.

evidence.note: General Counsel sits on ISRC committees and chairs the OLRC. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: CFRO reviews financial, tax and funding effects
steps.description: The Chief Financial and Risk Officer reviews valuation approach, tax structure, funding and liquidity effects and reporting implications, and gives a view.

evidence.note: CFRO chairs the Investment Risk Committee and sits on the ISRC. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Chair concludes and records the decision
steps.description: The CIO sums up the discussion and decides to approve, approve with conditions, defer for more work, decline, or recommend the item to the Board because it exceeds the committee's authority.

control.basis: Investment Management Authorities and PEC terms of reference: committee approval of new investments, dispositions and follow-ons

next.condition: above committee authority, recommend to the Board

evidence.note: PEC chaired by the CIO approves or declines; transactions above set amounts go to the Board. Shares are the author's estimates; the Board share matches about 3 Board items a month.

steps.name: Deal team answers the committee's questions
steps.description: The sponsoring team's director runs the extra analysis the committee asked for, such as a downside case, a partner check or a revised structure, and sends a supplement for the next meeting.

evidence.note: Tiered committees return deals for more work. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Draft the decision minute
steps.description: The secretariat writes the minute: decision, amount and price limits, conditions such as final diligence items or maximum leverage, and follow-up reporting, and sends it to the chair.

error.defect_description: Condition or price limit recorded incorrectly.

evidence.note: Committee minutes record decisions and are reported upward. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Chair approves the minute
steps.description: The CIO reads the draft minute, checks the recorded decision, conditions and price limits against the meeting, and approves it in the repository or corrects it.

control.basis: Documented approval record under the approval authorities for audit and the special examination

evidence.note: Chair sign-off of minutes is standard committee practice. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Record approval and notify deal team, Legal and Compliance
steps.description: The secretariat updates the pipeline system, sends the approved minute and conditions to the deal team, Legal and Compliance, and closes the item.

evidence.note: Approval triggers negotiation and closing. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Record decline and notify the deal team
steps.description: The secretariat records the decline and the committee's reasons in the tracker and pipeline system and informs the deal team, which tells the seller or partner.

evidence.note: Common committee practice. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Prepare the Board referral
steps.description: A TFM principal works with the deal team to turn the memo into a Board submission with a management recommendation and the committee's conditions, in the Board's format.

evidence.note: The Board's Investment Strategy Committee approves transactions as provided by the Authorities Policy. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: CIO signs the Board recommendation
steps.description: The CIO reviews and signs the Board submission and the board secretariat takes it for the next Investment Strategy Committee meeting or a special meeting.

control.basis: the fund's governing act s.34: the Board's investment committee performs delegated duties and approves discretionary manager engagements; transaction thresholds are set in the Board's Authorities Policy

evidence.note: ISC approves transactions above management authority; manager engagement approval is required by the Act. Times are the author's estimates.

exceptions.name: Incomplete memo
exceptions.description: A tax, legal, ESG or climate section or a sign-off is missing; the secretariat returns the memo.

exceptions.name: Deferred for more work
exceptions.description: The committee asks for a downside case, partner checks or a revised structure and the item comes back to a later meeting.

exceptions.name: Time-critical special meeting
exceptions.description: A bid deadline falls before the next regular meeting, so the secretariat arranges a special meeting with a short pre-read.

exceptions.name: Above committee authority
exceptions.description: The amount exceeds the committee's authority; management recommends it to the Board's Investment Strategy Committee.

exceptions.name: Item withdrawn
exceptions.description: The sale process moves on or the partner drops out before the meeting.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from memo submission to recorded decision
benchmarks.population: Management investment committees at large institutional investors

evidence.note: No published cycle time; the author's estimate from a weekly meeting cadence, a few days for the risk opinion and a two-day pre-read. Peer committees meet from twice weekly to monthly.
Eight regular meetings plus special meetings; most directors attended 12.

benchmarks.population: Investment Strategy Committee terms of reference

evidence.note: At least four times a year.

pain_points.description: Items wait for the risk opinion and the next weekly slot, which together take most of the elapsed time while the deal team has a bid deadline.

evidence.note: Risk review runs in parallel; wait times are estimates.

pain_points.description: Deferrals send items back for another full cycle, often a week or more, when a question could be answered between meetings.

evidence.note: Tiered committees trade speed for control.

pain_points.description: Senior executives spend hours each week reading long packages; the chair and members are a scarce resource that sets the pace.

evidence.note: The CIO chairs both the PEC and the PSC and members are senior leaders.

sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: The Board's investment committee performs duties delegated by the board, approves the engagement of investment managers with discretionary authority and oversees procedures to monitor investment policies; policies must meet a prudent person standard

assumptions: The committee is assumed to meet weekly with special meetings for bid deadlines; the organisation does not publish its cadence.
The secretariat role is filled by a TFM associate; the organisation file names no PEC secretary.

The members' review step carries the time of about four members other than the chair, Risk, General Counsel and the CFRO, costed at the TFM managing director rate; real members are mostly department heads at higher pay.
The deferral step uses pe_director as a stand-in for the sponsoring team's director; the organisation file gives PE, RA, CI and AE directors the same loaded cost.
Shares of items by sponsoring process follow the upstream volumes in the process map and typical conversion rates; department shares (PE 48%, RA 27%, CI 18%, AE 5%, CMF 2%) follow from them.
The risk opinion is an input to every item rather than a separate trigger, so its interface share is zero.

The process map lists only investment department SMDs, the CIO, a TFM MD, the CFRO, the head of Risk and the General Counsel; tfm_principal, tfm_associate and pe_director are added for the fit note, secretariat and deferral work.
Approval thresholds are not public (the Authorities Policy is not published); the Board share is set to match about 3 Board items a month in the process map.
